title: Tenali Raman and the Milking of the Bull

full_text:
In a whimsical and eccentric mood, King Krishnadevaraya decided to challenge the court with an impossible command:
'Within three days, my royal dairy must present me with a silver cup filled with pure, fresh milk milked from a sturdy male bullock!
If my ministers cannot provide bull's milk, each shall be fined five hundred gold coins!'

The ministers went home in utter despair. Male bullocks do not produce milk; it is a biological impossibility!
'The King has lost his reason,' moaned the Prime Minister. 'We must pay the fine!'

Tenali Raman smiled: 'Do not pay a single copper. I shall provide the King with his bull's milk.'

On the morning of the third day, the court assembled.
All the ministers sat trembling, unable to produce the milk.
Tenali Raman entered the hall, dressed in disheveled robes, his hair uncombed, looking utterly exhausted, panting and groaning as he walked.

King Krishnadevaraya frowned:
'Tenali! What has happened to thee? Why art thou so exhausted and untidy?'

Tenali bowed with an expression of immense, weary relief:
'Jahanpanah! Pardon my condition! I have spent the entire night acting as a midwife, assisting my elderly uncle who was in terrible labor, helping him give birth to a bouncing baby boy!'

The King stared at Tenali in stunned bewilderment:
'Tenali, art thou completely mad? A man giving birth to a baby?
Men do not give birth! It is an absolute, natural impossibility!'

Tenali Raman looked up with radiant, sparkling wit:
'Precisely, Your Majesty!
If a man cannot give birth to a baby because of the immutable laws of nature, how can a male bullock give milk?
Nature gave milk only to the mother cow, just as nature gave childbearing only to women!
When an Emperor commands his ministers to milk a bull, he asks nature to violate its own sacred laws!'

King Krishnadevaraya sat back on his throne, stunned for a moment, and then burst into hearty, roaring laughter!
'Ha-ha-ha! Tenali, thou hast caught me in my own trap of folly!'
The King canceled the absurd fine, rewarded Tenali with a gold medal, and praised his courage in holding up the mirror of reason to royal whims.
moral: An absurd demand can only be answered by demonstrating an equally absurd biological impossibility.
